proposals.name: Microlensed red background star
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens at low Galactic latitude is gradually magnifying a red background star, adding an achromatic, slowly accelerating rise on top of steady blended light. This explains the smooth >50-day monotonic brightening in r with a persistently very red g-r colour and the recent failure of fading SN/TDE forecasts in both bands.
proposals.predicts: It predicts an achromatic symmetric turnover and mirror-image decline to the pre-rise baseline, with g and r rising and falling by the same magnification factor and no colour evolution.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing of red source
proposals.idea: At low Galactic latitude a faint, very red background star has brightened smoothly for over fifty days and accelerated upward where supernova and TDE models predicted a cooling decline. An unseen foreground point lens is achromatically magnifying that star, with the constant component accounting for its unmagnified and blended baseline flux in each band.
proposals.predicts: The light curve will reach a single peak after day 0 and then decline symmetrically as the mirror image of its rise at essentially constant g-r color, rather than cooling, reddening, and fading asymmetrically like an explosion or TDE.

proposals.name: Drifting red template residual
proposals.idea: At b=-5 a crowded, highly reddened template likely contains a variable red star whose light leaks into the difference images at this position. A slow seasonal seeing and zero-point drift then grows that subtraction residual almost linearly in r with a much weaker, nearly constant g residual, mimicking a long, red, slow rise with no true onset.
proposals.predicts: It predicts the r flux will continue its linear drift, stay very red, and correlate with seeing or template changes or vanish on reprocessing with a clean template, rather than peaking and fading to zero like a supernova or TDE.

proposals.name: hidden Galactic microlens
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point mass in the low-latitude Galactic plane is slowly magnifying a red background star, producing the month-long achromatic brightening that supernova and TDE fits mistook for a fading peak. A constant per-band baseline accounts for the unmagnified source and blended field light on top of which the lens acts.
proposals.predicts: The light curve will peak achromatically and then decline symmetrically to its pre-rise baseline with essentially constant g-r, rather than decaying like radioactive or fallback emission.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing peak
proposals.idea: An unseen point lens at low Galactic latitude is slowly magnifying an intrinsically red background source, producing the 50-day monotonic rise to a plateau near peak. Unlike a supernova or TDE, the magnification is achromatic, so the red color is the source color and does not evolve from cooling ejecta.
proposals.predicts: It predicts a symmetric, achromatic decline back to the pre-event baseline at the same rate as the rise, with constant g-r color throughout.
